checked_sources: Independent bounded cyclic-ring calculation at n=3,5; 1≤s≤8
correctness.rationale: The two factors are integral symplectic shears with symmetric couplings. Modulo 2 the shift diagonalizes over a splitting field since n is odd, and the nonconstant mode with shift eigenvalue λ has distinct map eigenvalues λ and λ^(-1). A primitive n-th root forces odd part n, and the constant-mode unipotent block has order 2. The circulant Laurent representation is faithful: the matrices S^j have distinct shifts of one basis vector for 0≤j<n. In that ring, the Laurent sum for U_m hits each residue twice for m=2n and omits one exponent congruent to zero for m=2n−1. The even polynomial U_{2n−1} has zero derivative modulo 2, while differentiating U_{2n}=w U_n² modulo 2 gives U_n². Since Σ²=nΣ, shifting b to b+2 leaves U_{2n}(b+2)=0 modulo 4, and T^(2n)=I+2ΣI modulo 4. Nonzero Σ modulo 2 gives exact order 4n modulo 4. Squaring gives identity modulo 8: the unknown multiple of 4 contributes only a multiple of 8 because T^(2n)=I modulo 2, and Σ+Σ² is even. On the constant mode H has trace 4 and determinant 1, so H²=4H−I gives H⁴−I=8(2H²−H), not zero modulo 16. Raising this to odd n preserves the mod-16 obstruction, proving exact valuation three of T^(4n)−I. Squaring raises that valuation exactly by one, and raising to any odd power leaves it unchanged. Every identity exponent for higher moduli must already be a multiple of 4n, giving the claimed least exponent. This is the global order since a linear map fixes all vectors exactly when it fixes the coordinate basis.
residual_risks: The frozen 416-check output is a recorded result, not a replay during this review. The bounded independent test checks minimality only for its indicated sizes; it is not the basis of the all-odd-n result.

evidence: Nance constructs higher-dimensional examples by composing basis maps. Manolas–Floratos treat circulant equal-shear maps with a different trace and report no analytical odd-size base-order expression in the relevant comparison. Dyson–Falk theorem text was not available for inspection.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broad class of circulant couplings does not dominate the claim when the shear rule is restricted to a different matrix family. No inspected general statement yields the two low-modulus orders needed here.

evidence: The known recurrences and general squaring arguments do not give T^(2n)=I+2ΣI modulo 4 for this map. The frozen proof derives that congruence using the odd cyclic Laurent identity; the sharp constant-mode valuation separates mod 8 and mod 16. The equal-shear equation T(N;n)=(N/2)T(2;n) for dyadic N≥4 does not produce the plateau here.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Generic lifting determines subsequent doubling only after establishing the first exact valuation. The map-specific starting orders and plateau are the distinct content; a common nearest-neighbor coupling does not imply the claimed law.

evidence: The earlier equal-shear matrices have trace 2+c² on a Fourier mode; the unequal-shear map has trace 2+b. Every odd cycle has b=−2 cos(π/n) in (−2,0), so the unequal-shear map has nonreal eigenvalues, while real symmetric-coupling equal-shear maps have only real eigenvalues.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This rules out equality or real linear similarity to that equal-shear family. It is not a blanket exclusion of all modular or nonlinear conjugacies; the explicit known order laws also do not match the case at issue.

originality.rationale: The supported novelty is the exact all-odd-size dyadic matrix order for the unequal-shear nearest-neighbor map, especially its common mod-4 and mod-8 order and the exact onset of lifting. Equal-shear cat maps and generic matrix-order lifting are prior tools, not this order law. The closest inspected works differ in the update map or the underlying graph and size class.
residual_risks: Bounded search does not exclude an earlier exact unequal-shear or equivalent linear recurrence result. Dyson–Falk could not be checked in full; related modular conjugacies outside the tested family were not classified.

value.rationale: The recurrence order gives an exact return-to-identity time for all states of a natural spatially local symplectic torus update, uniformly in odd composite as well as prime circumference. The mod-4/mod-8 plateau distinguishes this arithmetic from automatic dyadic doubling; the uniform projector congruence explains it and the constant mode proves where it ends. This is more than an isolated numerical instance or a general lifting recipe.
residual_risks: The exact invariant does not give individual orbit-length counts, even-size or non-dyadic laws, or continuous dynamical behavior.
